title: A falsified sketch, caught by a same-text turn
story: A modified client commits A3's features as if A3 were an unrelated request, so the re-roll rule misses it and A3 is credited. A3 is drawn, and so are A1 and A2, which carry A3's text with its true values.
edits: The transcript's user entry for each prompt, read by the log reader 0.7 to 4.5 s after the hook (via log, same turn_key and lengths), as a real Claude Code client records it.
A3's f holds the sketch and template of 'add a dark mode toggle to the settings page header' under the device's K_feat. Its c is honest: it commits A3's real text, so the content reveal verifies.

CC5.basis: one device, whose scorer credits each slot to at most one project (SM 3.1)

CC6.basis: Stated, not recomputed: the live buckets are pkg/score over this device's events.jsonl, which the reveal holds in full, so the server's re-score is the same computation and every minute reproduces.

CC10.reason: no editor act in the submission

notes: The server re-scores from the bodies' f (DESIGN 6.2 D18), which say A3 isn't a re-roll, so the re-score credits A3 as the live buckets do and CC6 passes. Only CC8 sees the lie: A3's revealed text is A1's and A2's, and its committed th and mh aren't theirs (ledger-v1.md 10.8). The server can't tell which values are honest, so A1, A2 and A3 all fail.
DESIGN 7.3 and ledger-v1.md 10.8, as issue #15's decision rewrote them: CC8 reveals no keyed value and checks only what needs no key
